title: Implementation of Selected Aspects of the Climate Mobilization Act
plain_title: Enforcing the city's building emissions law
agency: New York City Department of Buildings
what_they_audited: Whether the Department of Buildings has taken steps to ensure private building owners comply with selected parts of the Climate Mobilization Act by the mandated deadlines. The audit covered November 2019 to June 2025.
background: The Climate Mobilization Act, enacted in 2019, aims to cut greenhouse gas emissions from the city's largest buildings 40% by 2030 and reach net zero by 2050. Its centerpiece, Local Law 97, sets emissions limits for large private buildings starting in 2024, and the Department of Buildings oversees implementation and enforcement.

findings.plain: While the department has made outreach efforts, including hiring third parties, it has not closely monitored either that outreach or building owners' compliance, so there is no assurance owners will meet the law's deadlines.
findings.quote: it has taken a hands-off approach to monitoring its outreach efforts and the building owners’ compliance with the requirements

findings.plain: The department could not substantiate its own outreach letters until after the audit's closing conference, and only a quarter of the addresses it supplied were on the list of buildings actually required to comply.
findings.quote: only 150 of the 602 addresses (25%) were on the CBL

findings.plain: A 2024 phone initiative to advise owners ahead of the first reporting deadline reached only 8% of the buildings required to comply.
findings.quote: DOB contacted only 1,118 of 13,269 (8%) of those required to comply.

findings.plain: In a survey auditors sent to 151 building owners, several respondents said they were unaware of the law or had never been contacted, and 20 of the letters came back undeliverable.
findings.quote: five respondents stated they were unaware of the CMA, seven said they were never contacted by DOB

findings.plain: The department refers owners to a service provider for help but does not follow up on referrals and has no documentation of what assistance the provider gave.
findings.quote: they do not follow up on the referrals

findings.plain: Auditors visited 55 buildings and found 24% had not posted the required energy efficiency label, while 31% of those that did post labels put them where the public could not see them, including one label inside a desk drawer. The department does not inspect for the labels.
findings.quote: found 13 (24%) did not have their energy efficiency labels posted as required

numbers.label: Covered buildings reached by the 2024 phone push
Outreach letter addresses actually on the covered list
Visited buildings missing the required energy label

recommendations: Contact building owners, especially those at risk of missing emissions requirements, and document that contact.
Reassess the resources assigned to contacting building owners about compliance.
Create a system to track referrals to the service provider, record what assistance was given and follow up on buildings at risk of missing emissions requirements.
Educate building owners on where energy efficiency labels must be posted.
Inspect buildings to verify a label is posted near each public entrance where the public can see it.
